Because government regulations created trust among consumers that the planes they fly and the medicines they take are safe.” 任何告诉你“我们现在承担不起监管，因为这可能会阻碍创新步伐”的人，都忽略了三件事。首先，正如牛津大学马丁学院新经济思维研究所执行主任埃里克·拜因霍克告诉我的那样，那些主张监管从本质上来说会扼杀创新、破坏市场的人“完全对历史一无所知”。他说，“良好的监管能够建立信任，而信任能够推动市场发展。你认为航空业或制药业为何能够如此迅速地发展壮大？因为政府监管在消费者中建立了信任，让他们相信自己乘坐的飞机和服用的药物是安全的。” Would the pharma industry be what it is today if people didn’t trust that the drugs they buy at the drugstore, without a second thought, have gone through a regulatory process? Because we have not yet had an A.I. catastrophe, people are going along with the hands-off approach. But when one happens, the pitchforks will be out for the “no-regulations” gurus, like Trump’s A.I. whisperer David Sacks — and for good reason. 如果人们不相信他们在药店里毫不犹豫买下的药物已经通过了监管程序，制药业还会是今天这个样子吗？因为我们尚未经历过人工智能灾难，所以人们目前对放任自流的做法表示顺从。但当灾难发生时，那些主张“无监管”的大师们——比如特朗普的AI顾问戴维·萨克斯——必将遭到民众的声讨，而这完全是有道理的。 Any company that creates an A.I. agent that does something bad in the world “should be held liable for it,” Beinhocker added. That is precisely what we did not do with the lords of the social networks, and we have paid a huge price for it. I was happy to see Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent tell CNBC on Monday that the Trump administration won’t give A.I. leaders a “liability shield.” That may be the best way to slow them down in the near term. I hope China does the same. 任何创造出在世界上作恶的人工智能代理的公司“都应为此承担责任”，拜因霍克还说。这正是我们在对待社交网络巨头时没能采取的措施，我们也为此付出了巨大的代价。我很高兴看到财政部长贝森特周一在接受CNBC采访时 表示 ，特朗普政府不会给人工智能领导者提供“免责保护伞”。这可能是近期内放慢他们脚步的最佳方式。我希望中国也能这样做。 Second, A.I. is not just a technology but also, as the computer scientist Craig Mundie has been saying, “a new species.” And like a new species, it is already exhibiting evolutionary properties. 其次，人工智能不仅是一项技术，正如 计算机科学家 克雷格·蒙迪一直所说，它也是“一个新物种”。而且，就像一个新物种一样，它已经表现出进化的特征。 “We’ve unleashed Darwin in silicon,” Beinhocker explained. The latest A.I. models have demonstrated a capacity for “self-improvement, self-replication and self-preservation. When you put those three things together, and their evolution happens at silicon speed, not human speed, you’ve got something extremely powerful, potentially dangerous and impossible to control.” “我们在硅基世界中释放了达尔文进化论，”拜因霍克解释道。最新的人工智能模型已经展示了“自我改进、自我复制和自我保存”的能力。“当你把这三点结合在一起，并且它们的进化是以硅基速度而不是人类速度发生时，你就得到了一个极其强大、具有潜在危险且无法控制的事物。” This becomes even more true as we begin to give our A.I. systems bodies in the form of robots, drones and vehicles. We must ensure that there is always a human in the loop — that they are never fully autonomous — until we can guarantee these systems will always operate in line with human well-being, Beinhocker added. 随着我们开始为人工智能系统赋予机器人、无人机和车辆等实体形态，这一点变得更加真切。我们必须确保始终有人类参与其中，确保它们绝不能完全自主运行，直到我们能够保证这些系统的运行将始终符合人类福祉，拜因霍克补充说。 Third, our president now runs the country the way he is said to have run the Trump Organization, which had to deal with multiple bankruptcies : There is virtually no regular policy process, interagency collaboration is weak, and on most days everyone in the administration just sits around waiting to see what the president posts on social media — often based on the last person he spoke to or something he heard on Fox News — and then tries to frame policies around it. (Thank goodness that at least Bessent, sources tell me, has done a deep dive into A.I. issues and has been talking to the Chinese. But whether he can herd the cats in this administration on this issue remains to be seen.) 第三，我们的总统现在治理国家的方式据说与他当年经营特朗普集团时如出一辙—— 该集团曾多次面临破产 ：几乎没有任何常规的政策制定流程，部门协作薄弱，大多数时候，政府里的每个人都只是坐等总统在社交媒体上发些什么——这些内容往往是基于他刚刚交谈过的最后一个人，或者他在福克斯新闻上看到的内容，然后再试图围绕这些内容制定政策。（谢天谢地，消息人士告诉我，至少贝森特对人工智能问题进行了深入研究，并且一直在与中国人沟通。但是，在这个问题上，他能否在这届政府中让这群各自为政的家伙们齐心协力，还有待观察。） My Times colleagues recently reported that sources close to Trump made clear that his dismissal of fears that A.I. could lead to mass extinction as a “hoax” is driven not by any technological assessment. It is said to be driven, they reported, by his fear that “if the artificial intelligence boom fueling the American economy slows down, the market could crash and recession could quickly follow.” 我在《纽约时报》的同事最近 报道 称，与特朗普关系密切的消息人士明确表示，他将人工智能可能导致人类大规模灭绝的担忧斥为“骗局”，这并非出于任何技术评估。他们报道称，其动机源于他担心“如果推动美国经济的人工智能热潮放缓，市场可能会崩溃，经济衰退可能会接踵而至”。 That kind of thinking is begging for trouble. Trump should be thinking about another president. Dwight D. Eisenhower famously said , “Plans are worthless, but planning is everything.” What he meant was that no fixed plan can survive all the unanticipated stuff that happens once a war or crisis starts to unfold. But if you’ve gone through a rigorous planning process — familiarized yourself with the depth of the problem and the kinds of things that could go haywire and built trust within your team — you greatly improve your ability to adapt on the fly. 这种想法简直是在自找麻烦。特朗普应该想想另一位总统的经验。德怀特·艾森豪威尔有句 名言 ：“计划毫无价值，但制定计划是至关重要的。”他的意思是，一旦战争或危机开始爆发，没有任何既定的计划能够应对所有突如其来的状况。但是，如果你经历了一个严格的制定计划的过程，深入了解了问题的本质和可能出错的环节，并在团队内部建立起了信任，你就能极大地提高临场应变的能力。 That is precisely what was missing in the run-up to Trump’s war with Iran, and we are paying a huge price for that today. Imagine what could happen if A.I. agents — a thousand times cleverer and more dangerous than Tehran or Trump — go off the rails. 这正是特朗普对伊朗开战前所缺乏的，而我们今天正在为此付出巨大的代价。想象一下，如果比德黑兰或特朗普聪明且危险成千上万倍的人工智能代理失控了，将会发生什么。 托马斯·L·弗里德曼(Thomas L. Friedman)是外交事务方面的专栏作者。他1981年加入时报，曾三次获得普利策奖。他著有七本书，包括赢得国家图书奖的《从贝鲁特到耶路撒冷》(From Beirut to Jerusalem)。欢迎在 X 和 Facebook 上关注他。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 美中元首峰会聚焦人工智能议题，但恐难有实质进展
description: ANA SWANSON2026年9月23日特朗普总统与中国领导人习近平去年在韩国。特朗普放宽了向中国及其他国家提供人工智能技术的限制。 Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times U.S. and Chinese officials are setting up a dialogue about artificial intelligence and a hotline to report national security risks from the technology. The United States is lodging criticisms with China over its companies’ copying American A.I. models. And a state dinner hosting China’s leader on Thursday is expected to be attended by some of America’s biggest A.I. and tech titans, including executives from OpenAI, Google and Nvidia. 美国和中国官员正在筹建一个关于人工智能的对话机制，并设立热线，用于通报这项技术带来的国家安全风险。美国正就中国企业复制美国人工智能模型一事向中方提出批评。周四为中国领导人举行的国宴预计将有美国一些最重量级的人工智能和科技界巨头出席，包括OpenAI、谷歌和英伟达的高管。 A.I. is front and center as officials from the United States and China meet this week in New York and Washington. But with technological competition between the countries so intense, and little consensus within the United States about the path forward on A.I. regulation, experts do not expect much headway. 本周美中官员在纽约和华盛顿会晤时，人工智能是核心议题。但鉴于两国之间的科技竞争如此激烈，且美国国内对人工智能监管的前进方向缺乏共识，专家预计会谈不会取得太大进展。 Concerns are mounting in the United States about potential threats from A.I., after warnings from A.I. researchers and incidents when A.I. agents escaped their training environments and hacked websites. Many U.S. officials worry that A.I. could enhance China’s ability to launch cyberattacks on the United States or crack military codes. Some believe the Trump administration should be doing more to limit China’s access to American chips and other A.I. technology. 在人工智能研究人员发出警告，以及出现AI智能体脱离训练环境并入侵网站的事件后，美国国内对人工智能潜在威胁的担忧日益加剧。许多美国官员担心，人工智能可能增强中国对美国发动网络攻击或破解军事密码的能力。一些人认为，特朗普政府应采取更多措施限制中国获取美国芯片及其他人工智能技术。 But President Trump has taken a laissez-faire approach. The only guardrails A.I. needs are a “strong and smart president,” he has said. 但特朗普总统采取了放任自流的做法。他曾表示，人工智能唯一需要的护栏是一个“强大而聪明的总统”。 “Whoever wins AI, WINS! We are leading now over China, and everyone else, and I’m going to keep it that way!” Mr. Trump wrote on social media on Monday. “I’m not going to stifle Growth, of something that will be bigger than the Industrial Revolution, or the Internet, itself.” “谁赢得人工智能，谁就是赢家！我们现在领先于中国，也领先于其他所有国家，我会让这种局面保持下去！”特朗普周一在社交媒体上写道。“我不会扼杀一项将比工业革命、甚至互联网本身更为重要的技术的发展。” Mr. Trump has opposed state regulation of A.I. And he has largely supported Nvidia’s selling the computer chips that fuel A.I. models abroad, relaxing restrictions the Biden administration set on providing the technology to China and other nations. 特朗普不赞成对人工智能进行国家监管。他也基本支持英伟达向海外销售驱动人工智能模型的计算机芯片，放松了拜登政府时期对向中国及其他国家提供该技术所设的限制。 The administration has granted a limited number of licenses this year to Nvidia to sell its H200 chip to China. Nvidia and its supporters argue that not selling the chips creates an opportunity for Chinese companies like Huawei to master their own A.I. chip technology. 今年，特朗普政府向英伟达发放了一定数量的许可证，允许它向中国销售H200芯片。英伟达及其支持者认为，如果不向中国出售这些芯片，就会给华为等中国企业提供机会，使其掌握自己的人工智能芯片技术。 The Trump administration is also widely expected to extend a trade truce with China that includes an agreement to pause sanctions on thousands of Chinese companies. 外界还普遍预计，特朗普政府将延长与中国达成的贸易休战协议，其中包括暂停对数千家中国企业实施制裁的安排。 Lawmakers are considering legislation that could impose tougher limits on the sale of chips and chipmaking equipment to China, but it is unclear if the bills have enough votes to pass. 议员们正在审议一项旨在更严格限制对华销售芯片及芯片制造设备的法案，但它能否获得足够票数通过，目前尚不清楚。 In a letter to Mr. Trump on Tuesday, Senator Elizabeth Warren, Democrat of Massachusetts, accused the president of accommodating the A.I. industry’s demands and said she was concerned he would double down on a “dangerous approach to artificial intelligence” in talks with Xi Jinping, the leader of China. 马萨诸塞州民主党参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦周二致信特朗普，指责总统迎合人工智能行业的要求，并表示她担心特朗普在与中国领导人习近平会谈时，会加码推行其在人工智能问题上的“危险做法”。 Ms. Warren said that Mr. Trump had used a previous meeting with Mr. Xi to advance the interests of tech leaders including Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive, who accompanied Mr. Trump on his trip to Beijing this year. She added that Mr. Huang would be called before Congress next year. 沃伦表示，特朗普曾利用此前与习近平的一次会晤来推动科技行业领袖的利益，其中包括英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋；黄仁勋今年曾陪同特朗普访问北京。她还说，黄仁勋明年将被传唤到国会作证。 “The American people expect you to press President Xi about the risks of A.I. and work with China and countries around the world to set rules and regulations for this technology,” Ms. Warren wrote to Mr. Trump. “美国人民期待你就人工智能的风险向习主席施压，并与中国以及世界各国合作，为这项技术制定规则和监管制度，”沃伦在给特朗普的信中写道。 Scott Bessent, the Treasury secretary, who plays a leading role in negotiating with China, has acknowledged the threat that A.I.-driven attacks might pose to U.S. stability and the financial system. 在对华谈判中发挥主导作用的财政部长斯科特·贝森特承认，人工智能驱动的攻击可能对美国的稳定和金融体系构成威胁。 Speaking after a meeting with his Chinese counterparts on Sunday, Mr. Bessent said that the United States and China had discussed creating a notification system for national security issues related to A.I. 贝森特周日与中方官员会晤后表示，双方讨论了建立针对人工智能相关国家安全问题的通报机制。 On CNBC on Monday, Mr. Bessent said that “the important thing was to start talking.” The sides agreed to meet on A.I. again, probably in two months in Shenzhen, and would consider “what the leading A.I. dangers are, whether it’s uncontrollable agents, whether it’s nonstate actors, and cyber nonstate actors in bioweapons,” he said. 贝森特周一接受CNBC采访时表示，“重要的是开始对话。”他说，双方同意再次就人工智能举行会晤，时间可能是两个月后，地点在深圳，并将讨论“人工智能最主要的危险是什么，是失控的智能体还是非国家行为者，抑或利用生物武器的网络非国家行为者”。 Some experts praised the idea of more dialogue on A.I. between the countries. 一些专家对两国就人工智能展开更多对话的想法表示赞赏。 “I think industry from both countries feels there’s a need to at least have some sort of A.I. governance conversation,” said Eric Zheng, the president of the American Chamber of Commerce in Shanghai. “我认为，两国业界都觉得，至少有必要就人工智能治理进行某种形式的对话，”上海美国商会会长郑艺说。 But many analysts have said that talks are more likely to result in an exchange of definitions and principles than concrete actions. The U.S. government asks American companies to submit their most sophisticated A.I. models for government review, but it has not made a similar request about the type of open-source A.I. models developed by Chinese companies. 但许多分析人士表示，会谈更有可能停留在交换定义和原则层面，而不是产生具体行动。美国政府要求美国企业将其最先进的人工智能模型提交政府审查，但并未对中国公司开发的那种开源人工智能模型提出类似要求。 Aalok Mehta, an analyst at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, said that the United States and China had some common ground. Chinese policymakers had also been thinking about A.I. safety and considering more intervention to gain insight into A.I. labs. 战略与国际问题研究中心分析师阿洛克·梅塔表示，美中确实存在一些共同点。中国的政策制定者也一直在思考人工智能安全问题，并考虑采取更多干预措施，以便深入了解人工智能实验室的情况。 But any A.I. talks will be complicated by the fact that neither country is likely to agree to anything that restrains its competitive ability, Mr. Mehta said in a panel discussion in Washington last week. American officials have also accused Chinese companies of stealing A.I. technology through distillation, and considered ratcheting up export controls on semiconductors. 但梅塔上周在华盛顿的一场小组讨论中表示，任何人工智能会谈都会因一个事实而变得复杂：两国都不太可能同意任何限制自身竞争能力的事情。美国官员还指责中国企业通过蒸馏窃取人工智能技术，并考虑进一步收紧对半导体的出口管制。 China feels the United States bears more responsibility in A.I., because it has the world’s most advanced models, Mr. Mehta said. That leaves “a very narrow set of issues that they can have productive conversations on,” he said. 梅塔说，中国认为美国在人工智能问题上负有更大责任，因为世界上最先进的模型掌握在美国手中。他说，这使得双方“能够展开富有成效对话的议题范围非常狭窄”。 Edgard D. Kagan, a senior adviser for the Center for Strategic and International Studies, said at the same event that fundamental distrust between the countries was likely to limit the information sharing that would be needed to have confidence that both sides were keeping their promises. 战略与国际研究中心高级顾问埃德加·卡根在同一场活动中表示，两国之间根深蒂固的不信任可能会限制信息共享，而要让彼此相信对方会信守承诺，这种信息共享又是必不可少的。 “China is deeply suspicious of anything that looks like it’s designed to lock in U.S. advantages,” he said, adding, “It will be very, very hard to come up with a mechanism that is anything more than symbolic right now.” “中国对任何看起来旨在固化美国优势的东西都深怀戒心，”他说，并补充道，“就目前而言，要设计出一种不只是具有象征意义的机制，将会非常、非常困难。” Ana Swanson报道贸易和国际经济新闻，常驻华盛顿。她从事新闻工作已超过十年。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

We are leading now over China, and everyone else, and I’m going to keep it that way!” Mr. Trump wrote on social media on Monday. “I’m not going to stifle Growth, of something that will be bigger than the Industrial Revolution, or the Internet, itself.” “谁赢得人工智能，谁就是赢家！我们现在领先于中国，也领先于其他所有国家，我会让这种局面保持下去！”特朗普周一在社交媒体上写道。“我不会扼杀一项将比工业革命、甚至互联网本身更为重要的技术的发展。” Mr. Trump has opposed state regulation of A.I. And he has largely supported Nvidia’s selling the computer chips that fuel A.I. models abroad, relaxing restrictions the Biden administration set on providing the technology to China and other nations. 特朗普 不赞成对人工智能进行国家监管 。他也基本支持英伟达向海外销售驱动人工智能模型的计算机芯片，放松了拜登政府时期对向中国及其他国家提供该技术所设的限制。 The administration has granted a limited number of licenses this year to Nvidia to sell its H200 chip to China. Nvidia and its supporters argue that not selling the chips creates an opportunity for Chinese companies like Huawei to master their own A.I. chip technology. 今年，特朗普政府向英伟达发放了一定数量的许可证，允许它向中国销售H200芯片。英伟达及其支持者认为，如果不向中国出售这些芯片，就会给华为等中国企业提供机会，使其掌握自己的人工智能芯片技术。 The Trump administration is also widely expected to extend a trade truce with China that includes an agreement to pause sanctions on thousands of Chinese companies. 外界还普遍预计，特朗普政府将延长与中国达成的贸易休战协议，其中包括 暂停对数千家中国企业实施制裁的安排 。 Lawmakers are considering legislation that could impose tougher limits on the sale of chips and chipmaking equipment to China, but it is unclear if the bills have enough votes to pass. 议员们正在审议一项旨在更严格限制对华销售芯片及芯片制造设备的法案，但它能否获得足够票数通过，目前尚不清楚。 In a letter to Mr. Trump on Tuesday, Senator Elizabeth Warren, Democrat of Massachusetts, accused the president of accommodating the A.I. industry’s demands and said she was concerned he would double down on a “dangerous approach to artificial intelligence” in talks with Xi Jinping, the leader of China. 马萨诸塞州民主党参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦周二致信特朗普，指责总统迎合人工智能行业的要求，并表示她担心特朗普在与中国领导人习近平会谈时，会加码推行其在人工智能问题上的“危险做法”。 Ms. Warren said that Mr. Trump had used a previous meeting with Mr. Xi to advance the interests of tech leaders including Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive, who accompanied Mr. Trump on his trip to Beijing this year. She added that Mr. Huang would be called before Congress next year. 沃伦表示，特朗普曾利用此前与习近平的一次会晤来推动科技行业领袖的利益，其中包括英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋；黄仁勋今年曾陪同特朗普 访问北京 。她还说，黄仁勋明年将被传唤到国会作证。 “The American people expect you to press President Xi about the risks of A.I. and work with China and countries around the world to set rules and regulations for this technology,” Ms. Warren wrote to Mr. Trump. “美国人民期待你就人工智能的风险向习主席施压，并与中国以及世界各国合作，为这项技术制定规则和监管制度，”沃伦在给特朗普的信中写道。 Scott Bessent, the Treasury secretary, who plays a leading role in negotiating with China, has acknowledged the threat that A.I.-driven attacks might pose to U.S. stability and the financial system. 在对华谈判中发挥主导作用的财政部长斯科特·贝森特承认，人工智能驱动的攻击可能对美国的稳定和金融体系构成威胁。 Speaking after a meeting with his Chinese counterparts on Sunday, Mr. Bessent said that the United States and China had discussed creating a notification system for national security issues related to A.I. 贝森特周日 与中方官员会晤 后表示，双方讨论了建立针对人工智能相关国家安全问题的通报机制。 On CNBC on Monday, Mr. Bessent said that “the important thing was to start talking.” The sides agreed to meet on A.I. again, probably in two months in Shenzhen, and would consider “what the leading A.I. dangers are, whether it’s uncontrollable agents, whether it’s nonstate actors, and cyber nonstate actors in bioweapons,” he said. 贝森特周一接受CNBC采访时表示，“重要的是开始对话。”他说，双方同意再次就人工智能举行会晤，时间可能是两个月后，地点在深圳，并将讨论“人工智能最主要的危险是什么，是失控的智能体还是非国家行为者，抑或利用生物武器的网络非国家行为者”。 Some experts praised the idea of more dialogue on A.I. between the countries. 一些专家对两国就人工智能展开更多对话的想法表示赞赏。 “I think industry from both countries feels there’s a need to at least have some sort of A.I. governance conversation,” said Eric Zheng, the president of the American Chamber of Commerce in Shanghai. “我认为，两国业界都觉得，至少有必要就人工智能治理进行某种形式的对话，”上海美国商会会长郑艺说。 But many analysts have said that talks are more likely to result in an exchange of definitions and principles than concrete actions. The U.S. government asks American companies to submit their most sophisticated A.I. models for government review, but it has not made a similar request about the type of open-source A.I. models developed by Chinese companies. 但许多分析人士表示，会谈更有可能停留在交换定义和原则层面，而不是产生具体行动。美国政府 要求美国企业 将其最先进的人工智能模型提交政府审查，但并未对中国公司开发的那种开源人工智能模型提出类似要求。 Aalok Mehta, an analyst at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, said that the United States and China had some common ground. Chinese policymakers had also been thinking about A.I. safety and considering more intervention to gain insight into A.I. labs. 战略与国际问题研究中心分析师阿洛克·梅塔表示，美中确实存在一些共同点。中国的政策制定者也一直在思考人工智能安全问题，并考虑采取更多干预措施，以便深入了解人工智能实验室的情况。 But any A.I. talks will be complicated by the fact that neither country is likely to agree to anything that restrains its competitive ability, Mr. Mehta said in a panel discussion in Washington last week. American officials have also accused Chinese companies of stealing A.I. technology through distillation, and considered ratcheting up export controls on semiconductors. 但梅塔上周在华盛顿的一场小组讨论中表示，任何人工智能会谈都会因一个事实而变得复杂：两国都不太可能同意任何限制自身竞争能力的事情。美国官员还 指责中国企业 通过蒸馏窃取人工智能技术，并考虑进一步收紧对半导体的出口管制。 China feels the United States bears more responsibility in A.I., because it has the world’s most advanced models, Mr. Mehta said. That leaves “a very narrow set of issues that they can have productive conversations on,” he said. 梅塔说，中国认为美国在人工智能问题上负有更大责任，因为世界上最先进的模型掌握在美国手中。他说，这使得双方“能够展开富有成效对话的议题范围非常狭窄”。 Edgard D. Kagan, a senior adviser for the Center for Strategic and International Studies, said at the same event that fundamental distrust between the countries was likely to limit the information sharing that would be needed to have confidence that both sides were keeping their promises. 战略与国际研究中心高级顾问埃德加·卡根在同一场活动中表示，两国之间根深蒂固的不信任可能会限制信息共享，而要让彼此相信对方会信守承诺，这种信息共享又是必不可少的。 “China is deeply suspicious of anything that looks like it’s designed to lock in U.S. advantages,” he said, adding, “It will be very, very hard to come up with a mechanism that is anything more than symbolic right now.” “中国对任何看起来旨在固化美国优势的东西都深怀戒心，”他说，并补充道，“就目前而言，要设计出一种不只是具有象征意义的机制，将会非常、非常困难。” Ana Swanson 报道贸易和国际经济新闻，常驻华盛顿。她从事新闻工作已超过十年。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 中日僵局难解，高市早苗向特朗普“求助”
description: 赫海威, 郭莉莉2026年9月23日日本首相高市早苗去年在东京与特朗普总统（未出现在照片中）会晤。高市早苗仍致力于说服特朗普维持在东亚的安全承诺。 Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times For almost a year, China has orchestrated a bruising campaign against Japan in retaliation for a comment by its prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, in defense of Taiwan. 近一年来，中国针对日本策划了一场猛烈的打压行动，以报复日本首相高市早苗保卫台湾的言论。 When Ms. Takaichi meets with President Trump in New York City on Tuesday, those tensions are likely to be high on the agenda. 当高市早苗周二在纽约市与特朗普总统会晤时，这些紧张局势很可能成为议程上的重要议题。 Ms. Takaichi, a longtime critic of Beijing, is expected to express her concern to Mr. Trump about China’s increasingly aggressive economic and security measures, according to two people familiar with her plans, including restrictions on the export of rare earth minerals. She will also emphasize her desire for a de-escalation with China, the individuals said. 据两名熟悉其计划的人士透露，长期批评北京的高市早苗预计将向特朗普表达她对中国日益咄咄逼人的经济和安全措施的担忧，包括对稀土矿产出口的限制。这些人士表示，她还将强调，她希望与中国缓和紧张局势。 The meeting between Mr. Trump and Ms. Takaichi, on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, comes a day before Mr. Trump is set to welcome China’s leader, Xi Jinping, for a state visit in Washington. Ms. Takaichi remains focused on persuading Mr. Trump to maintain security commitments in East Asia, including the more than 50,000 American troops stationed in Japan. 特朗普与高市早苗在联合国大会期间会晤，次日特朗普就将在华盛顿欢迎到访的中国领导人习近平。高市早苗的重点依然是说服特朗普维持在东亚的安全承诺，包括驻扎在日本的5万多名美军。 Kenneth R. Weinstein, Japan chair at Hudson Institute, a think tank in Washington, said that Ms. Takaichi had a strong relationship with Mr. Trump and that she would likely seek to reaffirm their alliance as a buffer against Mr. Xi. 华盛顿智库哈德逊研究所日本项目主席肯尼斯·温斯坦表示，高市早苗与特朗普关系密切，她很可能会寻求重申两国的同盟关系，以此作为对抗习近平的缓冲。 “She wants President Trump to send a clear signal to Xi Jinping that there is no distance between the U.S. and Japan on an array of critical issues,” he said. “她希望特朗普总统向习近平发出一个明确的信号，表明在一系列关键问题上，美日之间没有任何分歧，”他说。 Ms. Takaichi’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the tensions with China and her meeting with Mr. Trump. 高市早苗的办公室没有立即回应关于与中国紧张局势以及她与特朗普会晤的置评请求。 China and Japan have been at odds since November, when Ms. Takaichi said that Japan could intervene militarily if China were to attack Taiwan, a self-governed democracy that Beijing considers part of its territory. Beijing unleashed a wave of reprisals, restricting Japanese seafood imports, discouraging tourism to Japan and limiting the export of critical minerals to Japan. Chinese officials also cut off diplomatic channels to Tokyo. 自去年11月以来，中日关系持续紧张，当时高市早苗表示，如果中国攻击台湾，日本可能会进行军事干预；台湾是一个自治的民主政体，而北京认为它是其领土的一部分。北京随后发起了一波报复行动，限制日本海鲜进口，劝阻民众赴日旅游，并限制对日本的关键矿产出口。中国官员还切断了与东京的外交渠道。 The economic pressure has intensified in recent months, with tourism from China falling sharply — the number of Chinese tourists was down 59 percent in August from the previous year — and Beijing further restricting the export of rare earth minerals used in a range of essential technologies. 近几个月来，经济压力进一步加剧，中国游客数量锐减——8月同比下降了59%，北京还进一步限制了用于一系列关键技术的稀土矿产出口。 China in July exported 122 tons of rare earth magnets to Japan, according to Chinese customs data, a 52 percent drop from the year before. In August, China’s rare earth magnets to Japan were 17 percent lower compared with a year earlier. 根据中国海关数据，中国7月向日本出口了122吨稀土磁铁，同比下降52%。8月，中国对日本的稀土磁铁出口量同比下降了17%。 In recent months, Ms. Takaichi’s government has attempted to re-engage with China, sending delegations of lawmakers and business leaders to Beijing. 近几个月来，高市政府试图重新与中国接触，并向北京派遣了由议员和商界领袖组成的代表团。 去年在韩国庆州，高市早苗与习近平握手。预计两人将于11月在深圳举行的亚太经济合作组织论坛会议上再次会面。 Those visits have yielded some frank conversations. During one recent meeting in Beijing, Chinese officials peppered their Japanese visitors with questions about Ms. Takaichi’s plans to build up Japan’s military, asking if she was doing so with the goal of being able to defend Taiwan, according to a Japanese lawmaker who was present. The lawmaker asked not to be named because the meeting was private. 这些访问促成了一些坦率的对话。据一位在场的日本议员透露，在最近于北京举行的一次会议上，中国官员就高市女士加强日本军力的计划向日本来访者提出了一连串的问题，询问她这样做是否是为了能够保卫台湾。由于会议是私下进行的，该议员要求匿名。 During another recent visit, Masahiro Komura, a Japanese lawmaker who is a member of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party, pressed his Chinese counterparts on export restrictions and the recent detention of Japanese nationals on smuggling charges. Asked in an interview whether the talks had yielded any breakthroughs, he joked that it was a positive sign that no Japanese lawmakers were detained in China during the visit. 在最近的另一次访问中，日本执政党自民党议员高村正大就出口限制和近期日本国民因走私指控被拘留一事向中国同级官员施压。在接受采访被问及谈判是否取得任何突破时，他开玩笑说，在访问期间没有日本议员在中国被拘留，这就是一个积极的信号。 “The top priority is to continue the diplomatic relationship,” he said. “Without communication between two countries, both sides will become very skeptical, and a negative situation will escalate.” “当务之急是继续保持外交关系，”他说。“如果两国之间没有沟通，双方都会变得非常多疑，负面局势就会升级。” Chinese officials have used the recent visits from Japanese lawmakers as an opportunity to underline their unhappiness with Ms. Takaichi. In private, they have remained fixated on Ms. Takaichi’s remark on Taiwan, according to Japanese participants in the meetings, demanding that she retract it. 中国官员利用日本议员最近的访问作为机会，强调他们对高市早苗的不满。据参加会议的日方人士透露，在私下里，他们一直对高市早苗关于台湾的言论耿耿于怀，要求她予以收回。 China’s assistant minister of foreign affairs, Liu Bin, lectured a group of Japanese lawmakers when they met last week. He said Ms. Takaichi’s “erroneous remarks and actions” were the primary obstacle and that Japan should “demonstrate through concrete actions that it is worthy of the trust of its Asian neighbors.” 中国外交部部长助理刘彬在上周会见一群日本议员时对他们进行了严词告诫。他表示，高市早苗的“错误言行”是主要障碍，日本应“以实际行动取信亚洲邻国”。 In a meeting with another Japanese delegation in late August, Lu Kang, deputy head of the Chinese Communist Party’s International Department, said that “China-Japan relations are facing serious difficulties, and the root causes are clear.” 在8月底与另一个日本代表团的会晤中，中共中央对外联络部副部长陆慷表示，“当前中日关系陷入严重困难，症结是清楚的。” Ms. Takaichi’s advisers say she has no intention of backing down from her remarks, given her long history of support for Taiwan and widespread anxiety about China among the Japanese public. 高市早苗的顾问表示，鉴于她长期以来对台湾的支持以及日本公众对中国普遍存在的焦虑，她无意收回自己的言论。 Ms. Takaichi and Mr. Xi are set to cross paths again in November at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum meeting in Shenzhen. Neither side has commented yet on whether the two leaders will set aside time to meet one on one. 高市早苗和习近平将于11月在深圳举行的亚太经济合作组织论坛会议上再次碰面。关于两位领导人是否会安排时间进行一对一会晤，双方均未发表评论。 Lian Degui, director of the Center for Japanese Studies at Shanghai International Studies University, said the recent meetings between Chinese and Japanese officials showed there was the potential for relations to be repaired, depending on the messages from Ms. Takaichi’s administration. 上海外国语大学日本研究中心主任廉德瑰表示，中日官员最近的会晤表明两国关系有修复的潜力，但这取决于高市早苗政府发出的信息。 “If China finds the attitude acceptable, then Japan-China relations can move to the next phase of improvement,” Mr. Lian said. “The prerequisite for improving relations is for the Japanese government to admit its mistake.” “如果中国认为这种态度可以接受，那么中日关系就能进入下一个改善阶段，”廉德瑰说。“改善关系的前提是日本政府承认其错误。” The lack of a trusted intermediary between the two sides is another obstacle, analysts said. Under Ms. Takaichi, the ruling Liberal Democratic Party has lost the support of the Komeito party, formerly its main coalition partner, which had served as a conduit to China. 分析人士表示，双方缺乏值得信赖的中间人是另一个障碍。在高市早苗的领导下，执政的自民党失去了公明党的支持，公明党曾是自民党主要的联盟伙伴，并曾充当与中国沟通的渠道。 “What is lacking,” said Chen Hong, director of the Asia Pacific Studies Centre at East China Normal University in Shanghai, “is someone who can be taken seriously by Beijing and genuinely influence Takaichi’s decision-making.” 上海华东师范大学亚太研究中心主任陈弘说，“目前缺少的是一个能被北京认真对待并且能够真正影响高市决策的人。” In New York, Ms. Takaichi and Mr. Trump have a full agenda, including questions about trade, defense and Tokyo’s currency woes. Ms. Takaichi is expected to highlight Japan’s efforts to make good on a promise to invest $550 billion in the United States, part of a trade deal reached with the Trump administration last year. 在纽约，高市早苗和特朗普的议程排得很满，包括关于贸易、国防和东京面临的货币困境等问题。预计高市早苗将重点介绍日本为兑现在美国投资5500亿美元承诺所做的努力，这是去年与特朗普政府达成的贸易协议的一部分。 Japan has watched with concern as Mr. Trump has in recent weeks pressured allies like South Korea to provide support for the war in Iran; Ms. Takaichi appears eager to avoid the same fate. 最近几周，特朗普向韩国等盟友施压，要求其为伊朗战争提供支持，日本对此感到担忧；高市早苗似乎急切希望避免遭到同样的命运。 Ms. Takaichi also faces pressure at home to question Mr. Trump about his administration’s recent decision to sanction the president of the International Criminal Court, Tomoko Akane, a Japanese judge. The decision has stirred deep anger in Japan, and Ms. Takaichi has called it “very unfortunate.” 高市早苗在国内也面临压力，被要求就特朗普政府最近决定制裁国际刑事法院院长、日本法官赤根智子一事向特朗普提出质疑。这一决定在日本激起了强烈的愤怒，高市早苗称其“非常令人遗憾”。 It is unclear if Mr. Trump wants to get further involved in China’s dispute with Japan, though he has previously vowed to speak “Japan’s praises” to Mr. Xi. 目前尚不清楚特朗普是否希望进一步介入中国与日本的争端，尽管他之前曾承诺会向习近平“赞扬日本”。 Mr. Weinstein, the expert, said that is unlikely that Mr. Trump would ask Mr. Xi to “dial back the pressure” on Japan. 专家温斯坦表示，特朗普不太可能要求习近平对日本“减轻压力”。 “The best thing the president can do,” he said, “is continue to send the signal — by regularly consulting Prime Minister Takaichi — that the U.S.-Japan alliance is critical to the United States, Japan and the Indo-Pacific.” 他说，“总统能做的无非就是通过定期与高市首相磋商继续发出信号——美日同盟对美国、日本以及印太地区至关重要。” Hisako Ueno自东京、Pei-Lin Wu自台湾台北对本文有报道贡献。 赫海威(Javier C. Hernández)是《纽约时报》东京分社社长，领导时报对日本及周边地区的报道。在过去十年的大部分时间里，他一直在亚洲进行报道，此前曾任驻华记者。 郭莉莉(Lily Kuo)是《纽约时报》报道中国记者，常驻台北。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site
content: 赫海威, 郭莉莉 2026年9月23日 日本首相高市早苗去年在东京与特朗普总统（未出现在照片中）会晤。高市早苗仍致力于说服特朗普维持在东亚的安全承诺。 Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times For almost a year, China has orchestrated a bruising campaign against Japan in retaliation for a comment by its prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, in defense of Taiwan. 近一年来，中国针对日本策划了一场猛烈的打压行动，以报复日本首相高市早苗保卫台湾的言论。 When Ms. Takaichi meets with President Trump in New York City on Tuesday, those tensions are likely to be high on the agenda. 当高市早苗周二在纽约市与特朗普总统会晤时，这些紧张局势很可能成为议程上的重要议题。 Ms. Takaichi, a longtime critic of Beijing, is expected to express her concern to Mr. Trump about China’s increasingly aggressive economic and security measures, according to two people familiar with her plans, including restrictions on the export of rare earth minerals. She will also emphasize her desire for a de-escalation with China, the individuals said. 据两名熟悉其计划的人士透露，长期批评北京的高市早苗预计将向特朗普表达她对中国日益咄咄逼人的经济和安全措施的担忧，包括对稀土矿产出口的限制。这些人士表示，她还将强调，她希望与中国缓和紧张局势。 The meeting between Mr. Trump and Ms. Takaichi, on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, comes a day before Mr. Trump is set to welcome China’s leader, Xi Jinping , for a state visit in Washington. Ms. Takaichi remains focused on persuading Mr. Trump to maintain security commitments in East Asia, including the more than 50,000 American troops stationed in Japan. 特朗普与高市早苗在联合国大会期间会晤，次日 特朗普就将在华盛顿欢迎到访的中国领导人习近平 。高市早苗的重点依然是说服特朗普维持在东亚的安全承诺，包括驻扎在日本的5万多名美军。 Kenneth R. Weinstein, Japan chair at Hudson Institute, a think tank in Washington, said that Ms. Takaichi had a strong relationship with Mr. Trump and that she would likely seek to reaffirm their alliance as a buffer against Mr. Xi. 华盛顿智库哈德逊研究所日本项目主席肯尼斯·温斯坦表示，高市早苗与特朗普关系密切，她很可能会寻求重申两国的同盟关系，以此作为对抗习近平的缓冲。 “She wants President Trump to send a clear signal to Xi Jinping that there is no distance between the U.S. and Japan on an array of critical issues,” he said. “她希望特朗普总统向习近平发出一个明确的信号，表明在一系列关键问题上，美日之间没有任何分歧，”他说。 Ms. Takaichi’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the tensions with China and her meeting with Mr. Trump. 高市早苗的办公室没有立即回应关于与中国紧张局势以及她与特朗普会晤的置评请求。 China and Japan have been at odds since November, when Ms. Takaichi said that Japan could intervene militarily if China were to attack Taiwan, a self-governed democracy that Beijing considers part of its territory. Beijing unleashed a wave of reprisals , restricting Japanese seafood imports, discouraging tourism to Japan and limiting the export of critical minerals to Japan. Chinese officials also cut off diplomatic channels to Tokyo. 自去年11月以来，中日关系持续紧张，当时高市早苗表示，如果中国攻击台湾，日本可能会进行 军事干预 ；台湾是一个自治的民主政体，而北京认为它是其领土的一部分。北京随后发起了 一波报复行动 ，限制日本海鲜进口，劝阻民众赴日旅游，并限制对日本的关键矿产出口。中国官员还切断了与东京的外交渠道。 The economic pressure has intensified in recent months, with tourism from China falling sharply — the number of Chinese tourists was down 59 percent in August from the previous year — and Beijing further restricting the export of rare earth minerals used in a range of essential technologies. 近几个月来，经济压力进一步加剧，中国游客数量锐减——8月同比下降了59%，北京还进一步限制了用于一系列关键技术的稀土矿产出口。 China in July exported 122 tons of rare earth magnets to Japan, according to Chinese customs data, a 52 percent drop from the year before. In August, China’s rare earth magnets to Japan were 17 percent lower compared with a year earlier. 根据中国海关数据，中国7月向日本出口了122吨稀土磁铁，同比下降52%。8月，中国对日本的稀土磁铁出口量同比下降了17%。 In recent months, Ms. Takaichi’s government has attempted to re-engage with China, sending delegations of lawmakers and business leaders to Beijing. 近几个月来，高市政府试图重新与中国接触，并向北京派遣了由议员和商界领袖组成的代表团。 去年在韩国庆州，高市早苗与习近平握手。预计两人将于11月在深圳举行的亚太经济合作组织论坛会议上再次会面。 Those visits have yielded some frank conversations. During one recent meeting in Beijing, Chinese officials peppered their Japanese visitors with questions about Ms. Takaichi’s plans to build up Japan’s military, asking if she was doing so with the goal of being able to defend Taiwan, according to a Japanese lawmaker who was present. The lawmaker asked not to be named because the meeting was private. 这些访问促成了一些坦率的对话。据一位在场的日本议员透露，在最近于北京举行的一次会议上，中国官员就高市女士加强日本军力的计划向日本来访者提出了一连串的问题，询问她这样做是否是为了能够保卫台湾。由于会议是私下进行的，该议员要求匿名。 During another recent visit, Masahiro Komura, a Japanese lawmaker who is a member of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party, pressed his Chinese counterparts on export restrictions and the recent detention of Japanese nationals on smuggling charges. Asked in an interview whether the talks had yielded any breakthroughs, he joked that it was a positive sign that no Japanese lawmakers were detained in China during the visit. 在最近的另一次访问中，日本执政党自民党议员高村正大就出口限制和近期日本国民因走私指控被 拘留 一事向中国同级官员施压。在接受采访被问及谈判是否取得任何突破时，他开玩笑说，在访问期间没有日本议员在中国被拘留，这就是一个积极的信号。 “The top priority is to continue the diplomatic relationship,” he said. “Without communication between two countries, both sides will become very skeptical, and a negative situation will escalate.” “当务之急是继续保持外交关系，”他说。“如果两国之间没有沟通，双方都会变得非常多疑，负面局势就会升级。” Chinese officials have used the recent visits from Japanese lawmakers as an opportunity to underline their unhappiness with Ms. Takaichi. In private, they have remained fixated on Ms. Takaichi’s remark on Taiwan, according to Japanese participants in the meetings, demanding that she retract it. 中国官员利用日本议员最近的访问作为机会，强调他们对高市早苗的不满。据参加会议的日方人士透露，在私下里，他们一直对高市早苗关于台湾的言论耿耿于怀，要求她予以收回。 China’s assistant minister of foreign affairs, Liu Bin, lectured a group of Japanese lawmakers when they met last week. He said Ms. Takaichi’s “erroneous remarks and actions” were the primary obstacle and that Japan should “demonstrate through concrete actions that it is worthy of the trust of its Asian neighbors.” 中国外交部部长助理刘彬在上周会见一群日本议员时对他们进行了严词告诫。他表示，高市早苗的“错误言行”是主要障碍，日本应“以实际行动取信亚洲邻国”。 In a meeting with another Japanese delegation in late August, Lu Kang, deputy head of the Chinese Communist Party’s International Department, said that “China-Japan relations are facing serious difficulties, and the root causes are clear.” 在8月底与另一个日本代表团的会晤中，中共中央对外联络部副部长陆慷表示，“当前中日关系陷入严重困难，症结是清楚的。” Ms. Takaichi’s advisers say she has no intention of backing down from her remarks, given her long history of support for Taiwan and widespread anxiety about China among the Japanese public. 高市早苗的顾问表示，鉴于她长期以来对台湾的支持以及日本公众对中国普遍存在的焦虑，她无意收回自己的言论。 Ms. Takaichi and Mr. Xi are set to cross paths again in November at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum meeting in Shenzhen. Neither side has commented yet on whether the two leaders will set aside time to meet one on one. 高市早苗和习近平将于11月在深圳举行的亚太经济合作组织论坛会议上再次碰面。关于两位领导人是否会安排时间进行一对一会晤，双方均未发表评论。 Lian Degui, director of the Center for Japanese Studies at Shanghai International Studies University, said the recent meetings between Chinese and Japanese officials showed there was the potential for relations to be repaired, depending on the messages from Ms. Takaichi’s administration. 上海外国语大学日本研究中心主任廉德瑰表示，中日官员最近的会晤表明两国关系有修复的潜力，但这取决于高市早苗政府发出的信息。 “If China finds the attitude acceptable, then Japan-China relations can move to the next phase of improvement,” Mr. Lian said. “The prerequisite for improving relations is for the Japanese government to admit its mistake.” “如果中国认为这种态度可以接受，那么中日关系就能进入下一个改善阶段，”廉德瑰说。“改善关系的前提是日本政府承认其错误。” The lack of a trusted intermediary between the two sides is another obstacle, analysts said. Under Ms. Takaichi, the ruling Liberal Democratic Party has lost the support of the Komeito party, formerly its main coalition partner, which had served as a conduit to China. 分析人士表示，双方缺乏值得信赖的中间人是另一个障碍。在高市早苗的领导下，执政的自民党失去了公明党的支持，公明党曾是自民党主要的联盟伙伴，并曾充当与中国沟通的渠道。 “What is lacking,” said Chen Hong, director of the Asia Pacific Studies Centre at East China Normal University in Shanghai, “is someone who can be taken seriously by Beijing and genuinely influence Takaichi’s decision-making.” 上海华东师范大学亚太研究中心主任陈弘说，“目前缺少的是一个能被北京认真对待并且能够真正影响高市决策的人。” In New York, Ms. Takaichi and Mr. Trump have a full agenda, including questions about trade, defense and Tokyo’s currency woes. Ms. Takaichi is expected to highlight Japan’s efforts to make good on a promise to invest $550 billion in the United States, part of a trade deal reached with the Trump administration last year. 在纽约，高市早苗和特朗普的议程排得很满，包括关于贸易、国防和东京面临的货币困境等问题。预计高市早苗将重点介绍日本为兑现在美国投资5500亿美元承诺所做的努力，这是去年与特朗普政府达成的贸易协议的一部分。 Japan has watched with concern as Mr. Trump has in recent weeks pressured allies like South Korea to provide support for the war in Iran; Ms. Takaichi appears eager to avoid the same fate. 最近几周，特朗普向韩国等盟友施压，要求其为伊朗战争提供支持，日本对此感到担忧；高市早苗似乎急切希望避免遭到同样的命运。 Ms. Takaichi also faces pressure at home to question Mr. Trump about his administration’s recent decision to sanction the president of the International Criminal Court, Tomoko Akane, a Japanese judge. The decision has stirred deep anger in Japan, and Ms. Takaichi has called it “very unfortunate.” 高市早苗在国内也面临压力，被要求就特朗普政府最近 决定制裁 国际刑事法院院长、日本法官赤根智子一事向特朗普提出质疑。这一决定在日本激起了强烈的愤怒，高市早苗称其“非常令人遗憾”。 It is unclear if Mr. Trump wants to get further involved in China’s dispute with Japan, though he has previously vowed to speak “Japan’s praises” to Mr. Xi. 目前尚不清楚特朗普是否希望进一步介入中国与日本的争端，尽管他之前曾承诺会向习近平“赞扬日本”。 Mr. Weinstein, the expert, said that is unlikely that Mr. Trump would ask Mr. Xi to “dial back the pressure” on Japan. 专家温斯坦表示，特朗普不太可能要求习近平对日本“减轻压力”。 “The best thing the president can do,” he said, “is continue to send the signal — by regularly consulting Prime Minister Takaichi — that the U.S.-Japan alliance is critical to the United States, Japan and the Indo-Pacific.” 他说，“总统能做的无非就是通过定期与高市首相磋商继续发出信号——美日同盟对美国、日本以及印太地区至关重要。” Hisako Ueno自东京、Pei-Lin Wu自台湾台北对本文有报道贡献。 赫海威( Javier C. Hernández )是《纽约时报》东京分社社长，领导时报对日本及周边地区的报道。在过去十年的大部分时间里，他一直在亚洲进行报道，此前曾任驻华记者。 郭莉莉( Lily Kuo )是《纽约时报》报道中国记者，常驻台北。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site

title: 李在明接受时报专访，敦促美国放松对朝鲜的制裁
description: CHOE SANG-HUN2026年9月22日韩国总统李在明在首尔的总统官邸青瓦台与《纽约时报》交谈了约70分钟。 Chang W. Lee/The New York Times Breaking with decades of policy on North Korea, the president of South Korea, Lee Jae Myung, is now urging the United States to ease sanctions on Pyongyang in exchange for an agreement that it freeze its weapons programs. 韩国总统李在明正打破数十年来对朝鲜的政策，敦促美国放松对平壤的制裁，以换取其冻结武器计划的协议。 “I believe there is significant value in a trade-off between sanctions — which are not particularly effective anyway — and a stop to the development of additional nuclear weapons and intercontinental ballistic missile technology,” Mr. Lee said in an interview with The New York Times on Friday. “我认为，在制裁——反正这些制裁也不是特别有效——与制止进一步发展核武器和洲际弹道导弹技术之间取舍是有很大价值的，”李在明周五在接受《纽约时报》采访时说。 However unpalatable such a bargain may seem, the world has no realistic alternative, Mr. Lee argued. North Korea is increasingly brandishing its nuclear missiles against the South. It is no longer the isolated pariah that Washington has tried to tame through a mix of pressure and dialogue as the wars in Ukraine and Iran have altered the geopolitical landscape. 李在明主张，无论这样的交易看起来多么令人难以接受，世界没有现实的替代方案。朝鲜正越来越多地向韩国亮出它的核导弹。随着乌克兰和伊朗的战争改变地缘政治格局，朝鲜已经不再是一个被孤立的国际弃儿，被华盛顿试图通过压力和对话相结合来驯服。 Both Russia and China have re-embraced North Korea as a strategic partner, particularly after the North Korean leader, Kim Jong-un, deployed troops and weapons to support Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. That conflict, alongside American strikes in Iran, has only strengthened North Korea’s resolve to expand its nuclear deterrent. 俄罗斯和中国都重新拥抱朝鲜作为战略伙伴，特别是在朝鲜领导人金正恩部署军队和武器支持俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰之后。那场冲突，加上美国在伊朗的打击，只会加强朝鲜扩大其核威慑的决心。 朝鲜领导人金正恩一直受到俄罗斯和中国的拉拢。去年，他在北京的天安门广场与普京和习近平一起参加了一场阅兵式。 Still, Mr. Lee believes that President Trump is the only leader capable of drawing Mr. Kim back to the negotiating table. South Korean officials say Mr. Trump represents the North Korean leader’s best opportunity to sign a peace treaty for the Korean War, which never formally ended, and normalize relations with Washington. 尽管如此，李在明认为特朗普总统是唯一有能力将金正恩拉回谈判桌的领导人。韩国官员表示，特朗普是朝鲜领导人签署朝鲜战争和平条约——这场战争从未正式结束——并与华盛顿实现关系正常化的最佳机会。 Some analysts warn it is naïve to expect the two leaders to forge a substantial deal, but Mr. Lee asked what option is left but diplomacy. 一些分析人士警告说，期望两位领导人达成实质性协议是幼稚的，但李在明问，除了外交还有什么选择。 “Aiming for denuclearization under the current circumstances,” Mr. Lee warned, “guarantees that nothing will be accomplished.” “在当前情况下以无核化为目标，”李在明警告说，“保证什么都不会实现。” Once a freeze is secured, he envisions building trust through reciprocal incentives and concessions to eventually convince the North to reduce its nuclear arsenal. The ultimate goal would be to create an environment where Pyongyang feels secure enough to survive without nuclear weapons. 一旦冻结得到确保，他设想通过互惠激励和让步来建立信任，最终说服朝鲜削减其核武库。最终目标将是创造一个环境，让平壤感到足够安全，可以在没有核武器的情况下生存。 This week, Mr. Lee will visit New York, where he will present his vision for peace and coexistence on the Korean Peninsula to the United Nations. 本周，李在明将访问纽约，在那里他将向联合国提出他对朝鲜半岛和平与共存的愿景。 Mr. Lee spoke with The Times for about 70 minutes at the House of Eternal Spring, a tile-roofed banquet hall nestled within the Blue House compound, the traditional seat of the South Korean presidency. His predecessor, Yoon Suk Yeol, a conservative, moved the presidential office to the Defense Ministry headquarters before declaring martial law two years ago, starting a turbulent political period that ended in his impeachment and imprisonment. 李在明在常春斋与《纽约时报》记者交谈了大约70分钟。这座瓦顶宴会厅坐落在传统的韩国总统官邸青瓦台园区内。他的保守派前任尹锡悦在两年前宣布戒严并导致一场政治动荡之前将总统办公室迁到了国防部总部，尹锡悦最终受到弹劾和监禁。 Mr. Lee’s decision to return the presidency to the Blue House upon his inauguration 15 months ago was meant to signal a return to normalcy. During a recent university graduation, he posed for selfies with students — a stark contrast to Mr. Yoon, whose bodyguards tackled and gagged a student protester two years earlier. 李在明在15个月前就职时决定将官邸迁回青瓦台，旨在发出回归常态的信号。在最近的一次大学毕业典礼上，他与学生们自拍——这与尹锡悦形成鲜明对比，后者的保镖在两年前强行按倒并捂嘴制服了一名抗议学生。 李在明周五在青瓦台。他任内面临着国内外的政治挑战。 Chang W. Lee/The New York Times But Mr. Lee, 61, is facing his own problems. His approval ratings have nearly halved since April as many South Koreans blame his government for soaring home prices and a recent stock market crash​. 但61岁的李在明正面临自己的问题。他的支持率自4月以来几乎腰斩，因为许多韩国人将房价飙升和最近的股市崩盘归咎于他的政府。 He also faces mounting pressure from Mr. Trump, who recently called him ungrateful for refusing to back the American war against Iran. During the interview, Mr. Lee defended his stance on Iran, saying that South Korea’s Constitution barred him from deploying troops to a war already underway between foreign countries. 他还面临来自特朗普越来越大的压力，特朗普最近称他忘恩负义，因为他拒绝支持美国对伊朗的战争。在采访中，李在明为他在伊朗问题上的立场辩护，称韩国宪法禁止他向已经在进行中的外国战争部署军队。 The South Korean president is also seeking to defuse trade tensions with Mr. Trump. South Korean negotiators are racing to implement a deal struck between the two leaders last fall, in which Seoul agreed to invest $350 billion in the United States in exchange for lower tariffs on South Korean products. 这位韩国总统还在寻求缓解与特朗普的贸易紧张关系。韩国谈判代表正在争分夺秒地实施两位领导人去年秋天达成的协议，首尔同意在美国投资3500亿美元，以换取对韩国产品降低关税。 To placate Mr. Trump, South Korea may offer to build a gas power plant in Texas and eight nuclear power plants across the United States, according to people familiar with the matter. 据知情人士透露，为了安抚特朗普，韩国可能会提议在得克萨斯州建造一座天然气发电厂，并在美国各地建造八座核电站。 Mr. Lee insisted he was unfazed by Mr. Trump’s criticisms. “I fully understand that from his perspective, the U.S. president may make various remarks,” he said. 李在明坚称他对特朗普的批评并不在意。“我完全理解，从他的角度来看，美国总统可能会发表各种言论，”他说。 Mr. Lee hopes to leverage Mr. Trump’s enduring fascination with the North Korean dictator to convince the U.S. leader to restart stalled talks and de-escalate tensions on the Korean Peninsula. 李在明希望利用特朗普对朝鲜那位独裁者持久的迷恋说服这位美国领导人重启停滞的谈判，并缓和朝鲜半岛的紧张局势。 特朗普总统与金正恩的个人外交（包括2019年踏上朝鲜领土的一次会面）没有产生任何结果。 Mr. Lee hopes dialogue between North Korea and the United States would improve his own nation’s relations with its neighbor to the north, which have deteriorated in recent years. North Korea has demolished roads and railways that once linked the two Koreas while also adding minefields and other barriers along their already heavily fortified border. 李在明希望朝鲜与美国之间的对话能改善他自己的国家与北方邻国的关系，近年来两国关系已经恶化。朝鲜拆除了曾经连接朝韩的道路和铁路，同时还在已经高度设防的边境沿线增加了雷区和其他障碍。 By contrast, North Korea is moving closer to both Moscow and Beijing​. After supporting Russia’s war in Ukraine, the North has opened a bridge along its border with Russia and is about to open another one with China.​ 相比之下，朝鲜正在向莫斯科和北京靠拢。在支持俄罗斯在乌克兰的战争后，朝鲜在其与俄罗斯的边境沿线添设了一座桥梁，并即将添设另一座与中国连接的桥梁。 The collapse of inter-Korean communication has eliminated South Korea’s ability to serve as a mediator between Mr. Kim and Mr. Trump, a role Seoul played in helping arrange three summit meetings during Mr. Trump’s first term.​ Those meetings ended without agreement on ​denuclearizing North Korea. 朝韩沟通的崩溃导致韩国不再具备充当朝美调解人的能力，首尔在特朗普第一个任期内曾帮助安排了三次峰会。那些会议未能促成朝鲜无核化协议。 Backed by Russia and China and buoyed by renewed economic growth, Mr. Kim is no longer as desperate for a deal with Mr. Trump and now possesses greater leverage to demand more favorable terms​, analysts have said.​ Still, Mr. Trump has repeatedly expressed his desire to revive his personal diplomacy with Mr. Kim, often boasting of their “very good relationship.” 分析人士表示，在俄罗斯和中国的支持下，加上受到经济恢复增长的鼓舞，金正恩不再那么急于与特朗普达成协议，现在有了更多筹码来要求更有利的条件。尽管如此，特朗普一再表达他渴望恢复与金正恩的个人外交，经常吹嘘他们之间“非常好的关系”。 Last month, Mr. Trump unilaterally scaled back a major annual joint military exercise with South Korea, describing it as “hostile” toward Mr. Kim. North Korea, for its part, said that Mr. Kim retained “good memories and feelings about Trump” from their previous meetings. 上个月，特朗普单方面缩减了与韩国的主要年度联合军事演习，将其描述为对金正恩的“敌对”行为。朝鲜方面则表示，之前的会晤让金正恩对特朗普保留了“美好的记忆和感情”。 8月在靠近朝鲜边境的韩国涟川举行的联合军事演习，几十年来，美国和韩国一直在进行这样的演习。上个月，特朗普单方面缩减了一场重要演习的规模。 Mr. Lee is not alone in calling for a change in strategy to revive talks with the North. At a forum in South Korea last week​, Stephen E. Biegun, who led U.S. negotiations with North Korea during Mr. Trump’s first term, said the United States could negotiate a “slowing or freezing” of North Korea’s nuclear arsenal.​ 李在明并非唯一呼吁改变策略以重启与朝鲜谈判的人。上周在韩国的一次论坛上，曾在特朗普第一个任期内领导美国与朝鲜谈判的史蒂芬·比根表示，美国可以谈判“减缓或冻结”朝鲜的核武库。 Others are more skeptical about a breakthrough. Cheong Seong-chang, a senior analyst at the Seoul-based Sejong Institute, cautioned that Mr. Trump may be more interested in creating a diplomatic spectacle with Mr. Kim, such as a surprise visit to Pyongyang, to divert public attention from the prolonged war with Iran. Nor would achieving a lasting peace on the Korean Peninsula be Mr. Kim’s main concern, he said. 但也有一些人对此存在怀疑。总部位于首尔的世宗研究所高级分析师郑成长警告说，特朗普可能更感兴趣的是与金正恩制造外交奇观，例如突然访问平壤，以转移公众对旷日持久的对伊战争的注意力。他说，实现朝鲜半岛持久和平也不是金正恩的主要关切。 Mr. Lee says the current stalemate in relations is simply too risky to be allowed to continue, as North Korea is steadily expanding its nuclear arsenal. 李在明表示，目前关系中的僵局风险太大，不能允许继续下去，因为朝鲜正在稳步扩大其核武库。 “Our estimates suggest that North Korea is now capable of producing, or may already be producing, an additional 10 to 20 nuclear weapons each year,” Mr. Lee said. “Once it believes it has accumulated enough nuclear weapons and missiles to guarantee its survival, it will be tempted to export them to make money.” “我们的估计表明，朝鲜现在有能力生产——或者可能已经在生产——每年10到20枚核武器，”李在明说。“一旦它认为已经积累了足够的核武器和导弹来保证其生存，它就会产生出口这些武器以获利的想法。” “That will be a truly dangerous moment,” he said. “那将是一个真正危险的时刻，”他说。 在常春斋的李在明。 Choe Sang-Hun是时报驻首尔首席记者，报道韩国和朝鲜新闻。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。
content: CHOE SANG-HUN 2026年9月22日 韩国总统李在明在首尔的总统官邸青瓦台与《纽约时报》交谈了约70分钟。 Chang W. Lee/The New York Times Breaking with decades of policy on North Korea, the president of South Korea, Lee Jae Myung, is now urging the United States to ease sanctions on Pyongyang in exchange for an agreement that it freeze its weapons programs. 韩国总统李在明正打破数十年来对朝鲜的政策，敦促美国放松对平壤的制裁，以换取其冻结武器计划的协议。 “I believe there is significant value in a trade-off between sanctions — which are not particularly effective anyway — and a stop to the development of additional nuclear weapons and intercontinental ballistic missile technology,” Mr. Lee said in an interview with The New York Times on Friday. “我认为，在制裁——反正这些制裁也不是特别有效——与制止进一步发展核武器和洲际弹道导弹技术之间取舍是有很大价值的，”李在明周五在接受《纽约时报》采访时说。 However unpalatable such a bargain may seem, the world has no realistic alternative, Mr. Lee argued. North Korea is increasingly brandishing its nuclear missiles against the South. It is no longer the isolated pariah that Washington has tried to tame through a mix of pressure and dialogue as the wars in Ukraine and Iran have altered the geopolitical landscape. 李在明主张，无论这样的交易看起来多么令人难以接受，世界没有现实的替代方案。朝鲜正 越来越多地向韩国亮出它的核导弹 。随着乌克兰和伊朗的战争 改变 地缘政治格局，朝鲜已经不再是一个被孤立的国际弃儿，被华盛顿试图通过压力和对话相结合来驯服。 Both Russia and China have re-embraced North Korea as a strategic partner, particularly after the North Korean leader, Kim Jong-un, deployed troops and weapons to support Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. title: “习特会”最棘手议题之一：中国稀土出口管制
description: KEITH BRADSHER2026年9月23日北京的国家博物馆内关于稀土生产的展览。 Maxim Shemetov/Reuters China’s restrictions on exports of crucial rare-earth metals and rare-earth magnets remain one of the most difficult unresolved issues as President Trump and Xi Jinping prepare to meet this week. 随着特朗普总统和中国国家主席习近平准备于本周举行会晤，中国对关键稀土金属和稀土磁铁的出口限制依然是最棘手的未决问题之一。 For months, manufacturers in the United States, Europe, Japan and India have complained about difficulties in obtaining enough rare-earth metals from China, which dominates global production. The materials are essential for making products ranging from cars and wind turbines to semiconductors, computer displays and military equipment. 几个月来，美国、欧洲、日本和印度的制造商一直抱怨难以从中国获取足够的稀土金属，而中国主导着全球稀土生产。这些材料对于制造汽车、风力涡轮机、半导体、电脑显示器以及军事装备等各类产品至关重要。 China imposed export controls in April 2025 on seven kinds of rare earths and magnets made from them. It later announced a broader set of restrictions, now scheduled to take effect Nov. 10. And in a political dispute, China has slashed shipments of rare earths and magnets to Japan, disrupting supply chains that also serve American manufacturers. 2025年4月，中国对七种稀土及由其制成的磁铁实施了出口管制。随后，中国宣布了一项范围更广的限制措施，目前定于11月10日生效。此外，在一场政治争端中，中国大幅削减了对日本的稀土和磁铁出口，扰乱了同样服务于美国制造商的供应链。 All three issues — the existing controls, the Nov. 10 restrictions and the curbs on Japan — are expected to loom over the meeting between Mr. Trump and Mr. Xi, China’s top leader. There is little indication so far of how they might be resolved. 所有这三个问题——现行的管制、11月10日生效的限制措施以及对日本的出口限制——预计都将笼罩在特朗普与作为中国最高领导人的习近平的会晤之上。迄今为止，几乎没有迹象表明这些问题将如何得到解决。 Rare earths have become a critical trade issue between the two countries since Beijing introduced export licensing rules two days after Mr. Trump imposed steep tariffs in April 2025 on China and dozens of other countries. China’s rare-earth shipments slowed to a trickle, and some manufacturers from elsewhere had to cut output of their products. 2025年4月，特朗普对中国及数十个其他国家征收高额关税。两天后，北京出台了出口许可规定，自此稀土便成为两国间的关键贸易问题。中国的稀土出口量锐减，其他地区的一些制造商也不得不削减其产品产量。 The experience last year demonstrated the leverage China derives from its near monopoly on the production of the important materials. 去年的经历彰显了中国凭借其对这些重要材料生产近乎垄断的地位所获得的影响力。 The White House says China has not fully followed through on previous discussions about issuing more export licenses. Deliveries have “not been up to par of what we would expect, and that, I’m sure, will be a topic of discussion,” a senior U.S. official said at a briefing on Friday. 白宫表示，中国并未完全落实先前关于发放更多出口许可证的讨论。一位美国高级官员在周五的简报会上说，交付情况“未达到我们的预期标准，我确信，这将成为一个讨论话题”。 American and European business groups say shipments are frequently delayed or incomplete or never arrive. China’s Ministry of Commerce scrutinizes every export application. 美国和欧洲商业团体表示，货物经常延误、数量不足或根本没有运达。中国商务部对每一份出口申请都会进行审查。 包头的稀土冶炼厂。 “While most of our members report getting the majority of the rare-earth supplies they need, the restrictions around the sector have given many doubts about relying on China as a dependable long-term supply chain partner,” said Michael Hart, the president of the American Chamber of Commerce in China. 中国美国商会会长何迈可(Michael Hart)表示：“虽然我们大多数的成员报称获得了他们所需的大部分稀土供应，但围绕该行业的限制让许多人担心，还能不能将中国视为可靠的长期供应链合作伙伴。” Guo Jiakun, a spokesman for China’s foreign ministry, said on Monday that Beijing remained committed to maintaining stable and secure supply chains for critical minerals. 中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆周一表示，北京方面仍致力于维护关键矿物供应链的稳定与安全。 The restrictions set to begin on Nov. 10 present another challenge. Current and former American officials said the United States and China had discussed postponing the rules but had been unable to agree on how long such an extension should last. They spoke on the condition of anonymity because of diplomatic sensitivities. 定于11月10日生效的限制措施构成了另一项挑战。现任和前任美国官员表示，中美两国曾讨论过推迟实施这些规定，但未能就延期多长时间达成一致。由于外交敏感性，他们要求匿名。 The United States has proposed a delay of six months to a year as part of a broader freeze on American tariffs and other trade actions, the officials said. 官员们表示，美国提议推迟六个月至一年，作为对美国关税及其他贸易行动更广泛冻结计划的一部分。 Such a deal would push renewed trade tensions beyond the U.S. midterm elections while leaving the Trump administration time to press Beijing before the 2028 presidential campaign over its trade surplus, import restrictions and industrial subsidies. 此类协议将把重燃的贸易紧张局势推迟到美国中期选举之后，同时为特朗普政府在2028年总统大选前留出时间，以就贸易顺差、进口限制及工业补贴等问题向北京施压。 But Beijing has its own political calendar. The Communist Party is expected to hold its once-every-five-years national congress next autumn, when it chooses the country’s top leadership. China typically seeks to minimize disputes ahead of the gathering, meaning a six-month or one-year deal could expire at an awkward time. 但北京有自己的政治日程。中国共产党预计将于明年秋季举行五年一次的全国代表大会，届时将选出该国的最高领导层。中国通常会在大会召开前尽量减少争端，这意味着一项为期六个月或一年的协议可能会在一个尴尬的节点到期。 China has instead sought a halt to further American tariffs and other trade actions for the remainder of Mr. Trump’s presidency, current and former American officials said. Chinese officials have declined to confirm that position and claim that the export controls are intended to prevent rare earths from being used in military equipment. 现任及前任美国官员表示，中国转而寻求美国在特朗普剩余总统任期内停止实施进一步的关税和其他贸易行动。中国官员拒绝证实这一立场，并声称出口管制的目的是防止稀土被用于军事装备。 Mr. Guo declined on Monday to discuss a possible extension of the Nov. 10 rules. 郭嘉昆周一拒绝讨论可能推迟11月10日规定的事宜。 Those rules would impose controls on five additional rare-earth elements, including erbium, which is vital for fiber-optic communications in artificial intelligence data centers and transoceanic cables. Even before the rules take effect, China appears to be restricting or delaying erbium exports, industry experts said. 这些新规将对包括铒在内的另外五种稀土元素实施出口管制。铒对人工智能数据中心和跨洋电缆的光纤通信至关重要。行业专家表示，甚至在规定生效之前，中国似乎就已经在限制或推迟铒的出口。 国家博物馆内展出的磁性材料。 “You’ve had bottlenecks building up at several Chinese ports,” said Ellie Saklatvala, metals director at Argus Media, a commodities pricing firm in London. 伦敦大宗商品定价机构阿格斯的金属主管埃莉·萨克拉特瓦拉表示：“几个中国港口已经出现积压的情况。” The most difficult dispute may be China’s sharp reduction in shipments of rare-earth magnets to Japan and its near suspension of some particularly important rare earths, including dysprosium, which is widely used in magnets for cars and in the most advanced chips. 最棘手的争端或许是中国大幅减少了对日本的稀土磁铁出口，并几乎暂停了一些尤为重要的稀土供应，其中包括镝。镝被广泛应用于汽车磁铁及最先进的芯片中。 China began imposing the restrictions in December after Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi of Japan said her country could help defend Taiwan if China invaded. Taiwan is an island democracy that Beijing considers part of its territory. 去年12月，在日本首相高市早苗表示如果中国“入侵”，她的国家可协助保卫台湾之后，中国开始实施这些限制措施。台湾是一个实行民主制度的岛屿，北京将其视为自身领土的一部分。 China has generally handled the sales of rare earths with each country separately, and it is unclear whether Mr. Xi will discuss the restrictions on Japan with Mr. Trump. Its refineries produce about 90 percent of the world’s supply of four rare-earth elements widely used in oil refining, glass polishing and low-end magnets: lanthanum, cerium, neodymium and praseodymium. But military uses account for only a small share of global rare-earth consumption. 北京表示，其稀土管制旨在防止武器扩散，而非施加经济压力。然而，军事用途仅占全球稀土消耗量的一小部分。 The Department of Defense estimated in 2024 that American military demand accounted for only 0.1 percent of global rare-earth demand. title: 习近平如何看待“习特会”：占据政治优势、底气更足
description: DAVID PIERSON2026年9月22日今年5月，特朗普总统与中国领导人习近平在北京人民大会堂。 Kenny Holston/The New York Times When China’s top leader, Xi Jinping, and President Trump meet in Washington this week, the two men will be operating on vastly different clocks. 本周，中国最高领导人习近平和特朗普总统在华盛顿会面时，两人面对的政治时钟将大不相同。 The American president is constrained by the immediate demands of a midterm election in November and a grinding war. The Chinese leader is gearing up for a norm-shattering fourth term as head of the ruling Communist Party, that will keep him in power for another five years. 美国总统受到11月中期选举迫在眉睫的政治压力以及一场旷日持久的战争的牵制。中国领导人则正准备开启他打破常规的第四个中共中央总书记任期，这将使他继续执政五年。 For Mr. Xi, the disparity in political realities gives him an edge in maintaining the truce that the two countries reached last year. A renewed trade fight would hit American consumers right before the election — a risk Mr. Trump can ill afford. China’s economy is struggling too, but Mr. Xi answers to no electorate, giving him the patience to prolong the détente on his terms. 对习近平来说，两人在政治现实中的差异让他在维持去年达成的休战局面时占据优势。如果贸易战再起，就会在选举前打击美国消费者，这是特朗普难以承受的风险。中国经济同样陷入困境，但习近平无需对选民负责，这让他有足够的耐心按照自己的节奏，将这段缓和局面尽可能延长。 “Each of Xi’s face-to-face encounters with Trump in his second term would only have reinforced Xi’s prior conviction that Trump is leading an America that is dangerous but declining,” said Jonathan Czin, a researcher at the Brookings Institution who previously worked at the C.I.A. analyzing Chinese politics. “在特朗普第二个任期内，习近平每一次与他碰面可能都只会进一步强化习近平此前的判断，即特朗普领导下的美国虽然危险，却正在衰落，”曾在中央情报局从事中国政治分析工作、现为布鲁金斯学会研究员的秦江南(Jonathan Czin)说。 Mr. Xi, who will sit down for talks with Mr. Trump on Thursday, may be wagering that leaning into Mr. Trump’s preference for leader-to-leader diplomacy can insulate the relationship from flash points like the status of Taiwan, the self-governed island claimed by Beijing, and the competition to dominate artificial intelligence. 习近平将在周四与特朗普举行会谈，他的盘算或许是：顺应特朗普偏好的“领导人对领导人”外交模式或许能让两国关系免受一些敏感议题的冲击，比如台湾的地位问题（北京宣称对这个自治岛屿拥有主权），以及双方在人工智能领域争夺主导地位的竞争。 Keeping Mr. Trump at bay would give Mr. Xi breathing room to work on rejuvenating his listless economy, which has been weakened by a property crisis, high youth unemployment and excess production. It would give him time to rebuild the upper echelons of his military leadership, which he has hollowed out in a drive against corruption and disloyalty. And it would allow him to continue expanding his country’s industrial, technological and military strength for a future showdown with the United States. 让特朗普暂时不来找麻烦将给中国领导人喘息空间，着手提提振因房地产危机、青年失业率高企和产能过剩而陷入疲软的经济。这也将给他时间重建军队高层，此前他在一场反腐败、反不忠行动中对军队高层进行了大清洗。同时，这还能让他继续增强中国在工业、技术和军事上的实力，为未来与美国的对抗做准备。 Analysts say China benefits every time Mr. Trump’s attention drifts elsewhere. By quarreling with traditional American allies or sinking deeper into the war in Iran, Mr. Trump is weakening his country's global standing and pulling troops away from the Pacific. 分析人士说，每当特朗普的注意力转向其他地方，中国都会从中受益。无论是与美国的传统盟友发生争执，还是在伊朗战争中越陷越深，特朗普都在削弱美国的全球地位，并将军力从太平洋地区撤离。 “Xi would love to tell Trump, ‘Go on, stay the course,’” said Suisheng Zhao, executive director of the China Center at the University of Denver. “For Xi, Trump represents a window of opportunity for China, so his priority is to buy more time.” “习近平巴不得对特朗普说，‘继续吧，照这个路子走下去，’”丹佛大学中国中心主任赵穗生说。“对习近平来说，特朗普给中国带来了一个机会窗口，所以他的首要任务就是争取更多时间。” An Emboldened Xi Heads to Washington 习近平更有底气地前往华盛顿 Since first meeting Mr. Trump at Mar-a-Lago more than nine years ago — a gathering best remembered for being when Mr. Xi learned about U.S. missile strikes on Syria while dining on what Mr. Trump described as the “most beautiful chocolate cake” — Mr. Xi has had an extraordinary amount of time for a Chinese leader to size up his chief geopolitical rival. 自九年多前在马阿拉歌庄园首次与特朗普会面以来——那次会晤最令人记忆犹新的一幕是，习近平在品尝特朗普口中“最美味的巧克力蛋糕”时得知了美国对叙利亚实施导弹打击的消息，习近平拥有了一段对中国领导人而言异乎寻常的漫长时间，可以观察和判断自己的主要地缘政治对手。 Early in Mr. Trump’s first term, Mr. Xi was somewhat accommodating toward the American president. In 2018, his government agreed to purchase $200 billion in additional U.S. goods and services to offset a trade imbalance (though Beijing never fully honored that deal.) 在特朗普第一个任期之初，习近平对这位美国总统在一定程度上采取了迁就姿态。2018年，中国政府同意额外购买2000亿美元的美国商品与服务，以缓解贸易失衡（尽管北京从未完全兑现这一承诺）。 2017年，特朗普与第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普在佛罗里达州棕榈滩马阿拉歌接待了习近平及夫人彭丽媛。 Last year, Mr. Xi flipped the dynamic between the two superpowers. 去年，习近平扭转了两个超级大国之间的态势。 Faced with Mr. Trump’s Liberation Day tariffs, Mr. Xi was the only world leader who refused to back down, choosing instead to match his opponent with one sky-high tariff after another. Mr. Xi then reached for his ace card by throttling exports of Chinese critical minerals, or rare earths, which companies globally need for modern technologies. Backed into a corner, the Trump administration called for a truce. 面对特朗普的“解放日”关税，习近平是唯一拒绝退让的世界领导人，转而选择一轮又一轮高额关税针锋相对。随后，习近平祭出了杀手锏，限制中国关键矿产（即稀土）的出口——全球企业制造现代科技产品都离不开这些资源。被逼到困境的特朗普政府于是呼吁休战。 It was a payoff years in the making: a rare instance in which Beijing not only withstood U.S. pressure but turned the tables and forced it to relent. Beijing, as a result, is emboldened today and sees itself more as an equal to Washington, analysts say. 这是多年布局终于得到的回报：北京不仅顶住了美国的压力，而且扭转了局面，迫使其让步，这是罕见的。分析人士指出，这让今天的北京底气更足，也愈发将自己视为与华盛顿平起平坐的一方。 The Trump administration “thought they could use massive unilateral pressure to force China to make concessions. And that did not occur. In fact, the opposite did,” said Scott Kennedy, a researcher at the Center for Strategic and International Studies in Washington. 特朗普政府“原以为可以通过巨大的单边施压迫使中国让步。但事情并没有这样发展。事实上，结果恰恰相反”，华盛顿战略与国际问题研究中心研究员甘思德(Scott Kennedy)说。 “I think now this is Xi Jinping’s world and we’re all living in it,” he added. “我认为，如今这个世界已经是习近平的世界了，我们不过都生活在其中，”他补充道。 An Unstable Truce 并不稳固的休战 The superpowers should put limits on competition, Mr. Xi’s argument goes, to avoid what he has warned could be a catastrophic clash. To this end, he has pushed a formula he calls “constructive strategic stability.” 按照习近平的主张，两个超级大国应当为竞争设定边界，以避免他警告过可能发生的那种灾难性冲突。为此，他提出了一套称为“建设性战略稳定”的方案。 In practice, what this means is that Beijing wants Washington to accept boundaries on where it can challenge China. 落实到实际层面，这意味着北京希望华盛顿接受一定的边界，明确它在哪些地方不可以挑战中国。 In July, for example, when the U.S. Federal Communications Commission proposed a ban on Chinese-made humanoid robots, China’s Ministry of Commerce invoked the phrase, demanding that Washington roll back the restrictions to preserve “strategic stability.” 例如，今年7月，当美国联邦通信委员会提议禁止中国制造的人形机器人时，中国商务部就搬出了这一说法，要求华盛顿撤销限制，以维护“战略稳定”。 2025年，中国杭州宇树科技公司的一场机器人拳击演示。 American analysts view the slogan not as a serious effort at ironing out differences but as an attempt to get Washington to recognize China’s clout and back off. China could apply it to any new U.S. restrictions on chip exports or arms sales to Taiwan. 美国分析人士认为，这一口号并非真正试图弥合分歧，而是要让华盛顿承认中国的实力并作出退让。对于美国今后出台的任何芯片出口限制或对台军售，中国都可能套用这一说法。 “The truce is not constructive because little diplomatic infrastructure is being built,” Mr. Czin of the Brookings Institution said. “It is tactical rather than strategic. And therefore it is inherently unstable.” “这种休战并不具有建设性，因为双方几乎没有建立起什么外交机制，”布鲁金斯学会的秦江南说。“它是战术性的，而非战略性的。因此，它在本质上并不稳定。” Summitry is the Strategy 峰会外交是一种策略 Mr. Xi appears to have calculated that the best way to manage the United States is to engage Mr. Trump in high-profile summits rich in optics but thin in substance. 习近平似乎已经认定，应对美国的最佳方式就是与特朗普举行一场场备受瞩目的峰会——场面十足，实质内容却不多。 The planned meeting on Thursday will be their third face-to-face in less than a year, a pace that could continue with talks in November at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, and at the Group of 20 summit in Miami in December. 计划于周四举行的会晤将是他们在不到一年内第三次面对面会晤。这一节奏可能还会延续：11月在深圳举行的亚太经合组织峰会，以及12月在迈阿密举行的二十国集团峰会，他们都可能再度会晤。 “Head-of-state diplomacy is the cornerstone of China-U.S. relations,” China’s top diplomat, Wang Yi, told Secretary of State Marco Rubio in a call on Thursday. “元首外交是中美关系的定盘星，”中国最高外交官王毅周四与美国国务卿鲁比奥通话时表示。 特朗普上一次与习近平会见是今年5月在北京。本周的会晤将是两人在不到一年内第三次面对面会谈。 But beyond extending the trade truce, the meetings have produced few breakthroughs. China may agree to more agricultural purchases this week, but expectations are low on issues like A.I. safety or China’s trade imbalances. 但除了延长贸易休战之外，这些会晤几乎没有产生什么突破。中国本周可能同意增加农产品采购，但在人工智能安全或中美贸易失衡等问题上，外界的预期普遍不高。 That is by design, analysts say. Enticing Mr. Trump with the pageantry of summits he seems to relish lowers the risk that he may do something to derail relations — like greenlight a package of arms to Taiwan. 分析人士指出，这正是精心设计的结果。用特朗普似乎乐此不疲的峰会排场来吸引他，可以降低他做出某些可能破坏两国关系举动的风险，比如批准一揽子对台军售方案。 Tellingly, Mr. Trump has avoided criticizing China in the lead-up to the talks, even downplaying a Wall Street Journal report that China had supplied Iran with satellite images of a U.S. base in Jordan where three American troops were killed in an Iranian strike. 颇能说明问题的是，在会谈举行前夕，特朗普一直避免批评中国，甚至淡化处理了《华尔街日报》的一篇报道，该报道称，中国曾向伊朗提供美军在约旦一处基地的卫星图像，而三名美军士兵在伊朗对该基地的袭击中丧生。 The summitry will also serve a domestic purpose for Mr. Xi by burnishing his image at home as a global statesman, during a moment of economic anxiety for many Chinese. It is important for Mr. Xi to demonstrate that he can manage Beijing’s most critical bilateral relationship, analysts say. 这场峰会外交对习近平而言同样具有对内意义：在许多中国民众正为经济前景感到焦虑不安之际，这有助于他在国内塑造自己作为全球政治家的形象。分析人士指出，对习近平来说，展现自己有能力处理北京最重要的双边关系至关重要。 Mr. Trump is expected to greet Mr. Xi personally on the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland when his plane lands on Wednesday. The White House will host Mr. Xi and Peng Liyuan, the first lady, for a state dinner, the first such banquet since King Charles III and Queen Camilla visited in April. 预计特朗普将于周三在马里兰州安德鲁斯联合基地停机坪亲自迎接习近平。白宫将为习近平和第一夫人彭丽媛举行国宴，这是自今年4月国王查尔斯三世和卡米拉王后到访以来举办的首场国宴。 “Xi wants to be seen by the Chinese public as a highly respected, influential and consequential world leader — and nothing can top being wined and dined at the White House,” said Minxin Pei, a professor at Claremont McKenna College who studies Chinese leadership politics. “习近平希望，在中国民众眼中，自己是一位备受尊敬、极具影响力、举足轻重的世界领导人，而没有什么比在白宫受到盛情款待更能体现这一点了，”研究中国领导层政治的克莱蒙特·麦肯纳学院教授裴敏欣说。 “Xi cannot afford to be distracted by a huge confrontation with the United States,” Mr. Pei said. “习近平承受不起与美国爆发大规模对抗从而分散精力的代价，”裴敏欣说道。 Berry Wang对本文有研究贡献。 David Pierson报道中国外交政策和中国与世界的经济与文化交互。他从事新闻工作已超过20年。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site
